name: Keir Zhou
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “Books arrive damp more often from dry flats than owners like to admit.” On Saturday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Keir stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I erased three lines before I understood. I've written down the one I remember.
appearance: Keir has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a brown corduroy jacket with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. In conversation Keir draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Keir takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Keir can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To restore a penciled sentence before memory loses it.
family: Fernando Arendt is Keir’s older cousin. Keir picks the meeting place. Fernando sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *Two names on the chart*, Fernando says, “I kept a clinic letter because the doctor spelled our village correctly.”
connections: Georgia Kwan. The teacher wants the erased sentence restored before the class reads the copy.

reactions.response: Keir lets both readers identify the line privately before adding a name.
